When working with APIs, you need to understand how to make HTTP requests. Most APIs require you to send a request to a specific URL, and the server will respond with data, usually in JSON format. Before making any requests, you often need to authenticate yourself using an API key or a token, which proves you have permission to access the service.

It is also important to be aware of rate limits. Many APIs limit how many requests you can make in a given time period. If you exceed this limit, the server will reject your requests. Therefore, you should always include proper error handling in your code. This way, if something goes wrong—like a network issue or an invalid request—your program can respond gracefully instead of crashing.
